headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work to automate tasks for hours, integrates with desktop & apps
summary: OpenAI's new ChatGPT Work tool can automate complex tasks and workflows for extended periods, integrating with popular workplace apps and offering desktop file access.
details: OpenAI has released ChatGPT Work, a new tool designed to automate complex tasks and workflows for extended periods, promising to "stay with a project for hours if needed." This addresses previous limitations where automated tasks would stop after a few minutes.

Users are encouraged to test its capabilities on familiar tasks like budget analysis or sales meeting preparation. ChatGPT Work aims to automate entire workflows, from customer research to tailored marketing assets, while still requiring user approval for important actions.

The tool includes "Scheduled Tasks," an advanced version of cron jobs, to handle repetitive tasks on a schedule or triggered by events. These tasks can continue running even when users are away from their desk, with monitoring available via phone.

ChatGPT Work integrates with common workplace tools such as Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, and SharePoint through custom plugins. The desktop version can also directly access and modify local files or use a built-in browser for online resources.

The system automatically uses external resources when necessary, but users can force specific third-party tools with the "@" symbol. OpenAI emphasizes that access to outside apps and files can be controlled via its Compliance API or enterprise settings.

OpenAI is merging its coding-focused Codex app into ChatGPT Work, though Codex remains a separate "view" within the new ChatGPT app. The existing ChatGPT desktop app is being rebranded as "ChatGPT Classic," becoming a more basic conversational option.

ChatGPT Work is designed for more involved tasks than typical chat requests, which may consume more of a user's plan's included usage. Subscription plans, mirroring Codex's structure, can range up to $100 a month with credit-based usage limits.

OpenAI is aware of potential "sticker shock" from extended agent use and high token consumption. Enterprise and Edu subscribers can implement overall spend limits or set group/individual-level limits to manage costs for high-impact work.

This rollout coincides with the debut of the new GPT-5.6 model, which promises "stronger performance per dollar" for demanding tasks. This model is available in three tiers, with the highest performance tier costing $5 for a million input tokens and $30 for a million output tokens.

headline_marked: [[Two new ETFs explicitly exclude Elon Musk]] and his companies from investments
headline: Two new ETFs explicitly exclude Elon Musk and his companies from investments
summary: These new Exchange-Traded Funds, named Nasdaq-100 Ex-Elon Enterprises ETF and S&P 500 Ex-Elon Enterprises ETF, allow investors to avoid companies like Tesla and SpaceX.
details: Subversive Capital has launched two new Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) designed to allow investors to avoid companies associated with Elon Musk. These funds, named Nasdaq-100 Ex-Elon Enterprises ETF (QQNE) and S&P 500 Ex-Elon Enterprises ETF (SPNE), are now registered and will be tradable.

The ETFs specifically exclude Tesla (TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) from their portfolios. This addresses a challenge for investors who use broad market index funds, as SpaceX and Tesla are often included in major indices like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100.

The funds aim to provide capital appreciation through exposure to large-capitalization U.S. equity securities, while explicitly excluding companies founded, controlled, or led by Elon Musk, or with which he is primarily associated. This scope allows for potential exclusion of other Musk-linked entities in the future.

The creation of these "Ex-Elon" funds reflects a growing investor sentiment to avoid supporting Musk, possibly influenced by his public comments and controversies. Subversive Capital is known for other themed ETFs, including those mirroring stock trades by Democratic and Republican members of Congress.

While it's too early to assess their performance, these ETFs offer a direct option for investors seeking to align their portfolios with their personal values regarding specific public figures. They also introduce a novel approach to socially responsible investing by focusing on exclusion.
